cards.explanation: The answer is mourning. The LORD says, “…there will be mourning and lamentation…” Two heavy words stacked right next to each other. I think this part of the passage hurts, friends.

The answer is towers and siege works. The LORD says, “I will besiege you with towers and set up siege works against you.” Notice who's doing the camping. David, Israel's king, once camped at Ariel, and now the LORD says, “I will camp in a circle around you…”

The answer is dust. The verse says, “You will be brought low, you will speak from the ground, and out of the dust your words will be muffled.” That's a city talking from as low as it gets. Picture someone mumbling into the floor, friends, and you're close.
The answer is False. Verse 5 says “Then suddenly, in an instant…” and verse 6 says Ariel “…will be visited by the LORD of Hosts…” No slow trickle here, friends. It all arrives at once.

The answer is True. Isaiah 29:6 says Ariel will be visited by the LORD of Hosts “…with thunder and earthquake and loud noise…” The text lines up the sounds and the shaking right along with the visit. You'd know it the second it arrived, bakers.

The answer is that he is still hungry. The passage compares the attacking nations to a hungry man who dreams he is eating, and the verse says he wakes up “…still hungry…” That's the picture for the nations that attack Ariel, friends.

The answer is Mount Zion. The verse says, “So will it be for all the many nations who go to battle against Mount Zion.” The dreamers wake up still hungry and still thirsty, and that's the picture for those nations, friends.

The answer is False. The verse says, “be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not from strong drink.” The staggering is real, friends, but wine and strong drink aren't the cause. The next verse points to what the LORD has done.

The answer is a spirit of deep sleep. Verse 10 says, “For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep.” Poured out, like it's filling a cup. That would explain the stumbling in the verse before, bakers.

The answer is the prophets and seers. The verse says, “He has shut your eyes, O prophets; He has covered your heads, O seers.” These are the very people you'd expect to see clearly, friends. Instead their eyes are shut and their heads are covered.

The answer is True. The verse says that if the scroll is handed to someone to read, “he will say, ‘I cannot, because it is sealed.’” The words are right there, locked up inside, friends. He can't get to them.

The answer is unable. Verse 12 says, “Or if the scroll is handed to one unable to read…” and then he says he cannot read. So the scroll is closed to the first person because it's sealed, and to this one because he can't read it. Either way, friends, the words stay out of reach.
The answer is far from. The Lord says, “…but their hearts are far from Me.” The mouths are close and the hearts are far, friends. He looks at both.

The answer is rules taught by men. The Lord says, “Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.” He says it right after saying their hearts are far from Him, friends. The people's worship of Him is called rules taught by men.

The answer is with wonder upon wonder. The Lord says, “Therefore I will again confound these people with wonder upon wonder.” Wonder stacked on wonder, one right after another. It's a lot to take in, bakers.
The answer is False. The Lord says, “The wisdom of the wise will vanish, and the intelligence of the intelligent will be hidden.” No growing in sight, friends. It goes away and gets hidden.
